summary: Eight observational carob case-study identities and source-backed summaries, retaining farm places, management phases, conditional findings and existing evidence.

topics.label: Drip irrigation
topics.description: Water delivery by a drip system. The reviewed Las Labores case documents deficit drip irrigation from May to September, with a seasonal total rather than an event dose. That farm example does not define a universal operating schedule, water requirement or establishment prescription for other species, soils or sites.

topics.label: Huerta Los Tamayos · Case study
topics.description:
An observational cultivation case at Huerta Los Tamayos in Prado del Rey, Cádiz, documents carob planting to diversify a traditional olive grove and enrich a sparse holm-oak dehesa alongside sheep grazing. Plantings in 1992 and five years later used nursery stock, manual holes, shelters, formative pruning and subsequent grafting with local cultivars. Establishment watering and hay mulch supported the initial phase; the stated tank capacity is distinct from the amount supplied per plant.

The account describes the stand in 2024 as mature trees integrated with the older oaks. Production showed alternate bearing, and local cultivars selected for livestock feed favoured pulp rather than seed yield relative to nearby populations. These are observations from a long-managed farm, not a controlled estimate of which intervention caused establishment or production. The wetter Cádiz setting and historical management differ from semi-arid Almería restoration. A quantified initial survival rate and a controlled comparison are not reported in the reviewed material.

topics.label: Los Lirios · Case study
topics.description:
An observational case at Los Lirios, Gaucín, distinguishes older carob afforestation and dehesa management from a separate intensive mother-plant plot established in 2023 to provide grafting material. The older planting received no establishment irrigation. In contrast, the one-hectare mother-plant plot used nursery plants, close regular spacing, grafting and frequent irrigation from April to October. These watering histories must remain separate.

The account describes an established older stand with many male trees intended for later grafting. The young mother-plant plot was reported to have no losses and good growth at the source’s observation point. Expectations for production after further grafting were forecasts, not measured future harvests. Fruit observations compare selected areas and do not establish that intensive irrigation or grafting alone caused the differences. A controlled survival comparison and the date of every observation are not reported in the reviewed material. The intensive mother-plant practice is not a general dryland restoration prescription.

topics.label: El Triguero · Case study
topics.description:
An observational establishment case at El Triguero in Carmona, Sevilla, describes conversion of low-productivity rainfed cereal land to extensive carob planting in autumn 2023. Shallow soils and sloping terrain formed the site constraints. Preparation combined ploughing, crossed subsoiling and manual holes; nursery trees received stakes, perforated shelters and monthly emergency watering. Planned grafting and subsequent pruning were intended to develop the plantation.

The source describes a plantation still developing for grafting, rather than reporting a completed production assessment. Grafting expected in autumn 2024 remains a document-stated plan unless independently evidenced; its calendar date is not proof it occurred. A measured survival percentage, yield and comparative treatment result are not reported in the reviewed material. The emergency water statement does not specify its calendar months or overall duration, so neither a seasonal total nor an ongoing schedule is inferred. This case documents practices and early status, not an experimental demonstration of their effectiveness.

topics.label: Buenavista · Case study
topics.description:
An observational intensive-cultivation case at Buenavista in Posadas, Córdoba, documents phased conversion of cereal land to a mechanisable carob plantation. Phases planted in autumn 2022 and 2023 used different stock and grafting arrangements. Soil preparation included large excavated holes and cured cow manure; selected cultivars and hermaphrodite pollinizers were combined with pruning, inter-row management and establishment irrigation during the first two summers.

At the account’s observation point, the first phase was grafted and the second was in its first year after planting. Production had not yet been measured; entry into production in three to four years was an expectation. The deeper, wetter site and production-oriented inputs distinguish this case from low-input restoration in Almería. The generic MP4 annual area-based irrigation allocation is not a measured Buenavista event dose. Missing event counts cannot be supplied by converting that allocation. No controlled estimate of the separate effects of manure, cultivar choice or irrigation is reported.

topics.label: Las Labores · Case study
topics.description:
An observational restoration case at Las Labores in Albox, Almería, documents carob replacing declining almond and olive in a shallow, rocky and dry setting. Planting began in 2010 in areas of dead almond trees, using manual holes, nursery stock, shelters, formative pruning and later local hermaphrodite grafts. Deficit drip irrigation from May to September is reported as a seasonal total of 400 litres per plant; the number of events and event dose are not supplied.

The handbook reports few losses, trees in good condition and successful grafting, while retaining alternate bearing. It does not provide a controlled comparison or a quantified survival percentage. Its chronology is inconsistent: autumn-2024 grafting is stated alongside production four years after grafting and a summer-2023 fruit table. Those statements are preserved as unresolved rather than forced into a single timeline. This watered, managed farm example must not be conflated with the separate MR1 model table’s no-irrigation guidance or treated as an adopted watering plan.

topics.label: El Rano farm · Case study
topics.description:
An observational cultivation case at El Rano in Ubrique, Cádiz, describes long-standing carob use within a livestock finca. Accessible trees were grafted with local cultivars and surrounding vegetation cleared, while difficult rocky areas remained seminatural. Carob harvest was integrated with grazing, and naturally dispersed young trees were candidates for later grafting. The checked case heading identifies Ubrique; earlier extraction notes that left the municipality open have a narrower historical review scope.

The account reports irregularly distributed mature trees and broadly stable crops with some alternate bearing. Its summer-2023 grafted/natural fruit comparison describes differing pod and seed characteristics without demonstrating a causal grafting benefit. Rainfall is inconsistent within the source: the narrative gives 800–1200 mm/year and the table 1200–1600. Neither range is silently selected. Irrigation quantities, a controlled establishment comparison and a quantified initial survival rate are not reported in the reviewed material. This is a relatively wetter cultivation case, not an Almería MR2 restoration trial.

topics.label: La Alcantarilla demonstration parcel · Case study
topics.description:
An observational MR2 demonstration case at La Alcantarilla in Mojácar, Almería, describes a seminatural carob population around houses and a stream in an area with low rainfall. Planting extended irregularly along paths, irrigation channels and watercourses. The handbook describes lentisco and acebuche establishing under carob protection, with little management beyond fruit collection.

The useful result is the observed development of associated vegetation in this setting, rather than a quantified establishment experiment. Fruit production was small or absent in many years despite some good crops and moderate alternate bearing. The fruit table records harvest observations but gives no sample size establishing a general yield effect. A controlled comparison, planting survival percentage, implementation chronology and irrigation regime are not reported in the reviewed material. General MR2 construction, planting and support-water recommendations on the preceding page must not be treated as a verified list of works carried out at this particular site.

topics.label: La Tórtola · Case study
topics.description:
An observational MR2 case at La Tórtola in Níjar, Almería, describes a naturalized carob population associated with earlier farming and livestock use. After those activities were abandoned, lentisco and acebuche established with the carob, producing vegetation described as more luxuriant than in neighbouring areas. The source characterizes the stand as naturalized and without cultural treatments, rather than documenting a new engineered planting intervention.

Trees varied considerably in size, with very strong alternate bearing and practically no fruit production. The case therefore illustrates a distinction between vegetation development and production objectives; it does not demonstrate that abandonment or any species combination causes a quantified restoration benefit. Potential lentisco/jujube scrub also remains distinct from the surrounding esparto-dominated current landscape. An establishment date, controlled comparison, survival percentage and irrigation quantity/frequency are not reported in the reviewed material. Absence of a stated watering regime must not be converted into a zero-water requirement.

findings.label: Huerta Los Tamayos: a site-specific watering regime
findings.text: 50–80 L/plant/event; three summer waterings during the first two years. Young 40–50 cm forest nursery stock in dehesa/olive enrichment; 40 cm holes, shelters and hay mulch. The 2000 L tank is equipment capacity, not a plant dose.

findings.label: Los Lirios: a site-specific watering regime
findings.text: 50 L/plant/event three times weekly from April to October. Intensive one-hectare mother-plant plot established in 2023 at Los Lirios; 2 × 4 m, 1250 trees/ha, 1 m stock. The older afforestation on the same finca received no establishment irrigation; preserve both contexts.

findings.text: 50 L/plant/event, monthly emergency watering. MP3 extensive planting at Carmona in autumn 2023; 1 m plants, 4 × 8 m spacing, 312 trees/ha, 30 ha, soil depth <50 cm. Calendar months and duration of this emergency regime are not specified.

findings.label: Buenavista: intensive production differs from restoration
findings.text: The case in Posadas has rainfall 600–800 mm/year and deeper soils, uses 1 m cubic holes with a 50% cured-cow-manure mixture, and phases planted in autumn 2022/2023. Selected cultivars include Sayalonga, Alexia, P14 and P17, with 10% of the two hermaphrodite cultivars for pollination. Production was not yet measured; the source anticipates 3–4 years. These practices are not recommendations for Almería restoration.

findings.label: Las Labores: dryland crops and a restoration transition
findings.text: Las Labores (Albox) has 200–400 mm annual rainfall, Mediterranean IV1 climate, coldest-month minimum 2–4°C, warmest-month maximum 32–36°C, annual mean 17–19°C, evapotranspiration 900–1000 mm/year, shallow calcareous soils and rocky outcrops. The landscape is dominated by dryland woody crops. Carob was planted in 2010 at 6 × 6 m in areas of dead almond trees, as almond and olive productivity declined.

findings.label: Las Labores: planting, protection and grafting
findings.text: The case uses nursery plants about 1 m high, manual 40 × 40 × 40 cm holes, perforated 60 cm shelters, tutors, formative pruning and tractor cultivation every three years. It reports grafting local hermaphrodite cultivars in autumn 2024. These are case practices, distinct from the MR1 summary table.

findings.label: El Rano: historical management and inconsistent rainfall
findings.text: El Rano (Ubrique, Cádiz) is a longstanding livestock finca with carob, wild olive and family crops. Accessible carobs are grafted and cleared; difficult areas remain seminatural. The narrative gives 800–1200 mm/year rainfall, while Table 5.17 gives 1200–1600. Do not silently choose one or classify it as an Almería case.

findings.label: La Alcantarilla: carob facilitates observed shrub establishment
findings.text: A seminatural carob population around houses and a stream has expanded irregularly along paths, irrigation channels and streams. Lentisco and acebuche have established under carob protection. Care is limited mainly to fruit collection. Alternate bearing is moderate, but crops are small or absent in most years. This is not a quantified planting trial.

findings.label: La Tórtola: naturalized vegetation and very low production
findings.text: Abandonment of earlier agricultural and livestock activity allowed lentisco and acebuche to establish with carob, creating more luxuriant vegetation than surrounding areas. The population is described as fully naturalized without cultural treatments. Trees range from about 1 to 10 m, with variable diameters, very high alternate bearing and practically no production. Irrigation quantity/frequency is not specified; do not turn absence of a stated regime into zero.

findings.text: The source’s 2024 account describes mature carob integrated with older holm oaks after enrichment plantings in 1992 and five years later.
